# Local helper membership audit for #451

Verified 2026-11-25. Inventory baseline `b85adf202`, source `7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a`. The historical manifest has 24 distinct Triton-distributed paths at this pin. The current manifest has 18. The source repository was clean, its HEAD equaled the pin, and all 24 local file hashes matched the corresponding Git blobs. Both manifests were run through VeriTile’s `scripts/census/scan.py:scan_source` and `scripts/census/report.py:kernels_of`. Each membership is one file-qualified kernel with a reachable local helper of the indicated decorator, however many calls it reaches. Other decorators may occur as intermediate calls. Imported functions and host call-graph reachability are outside this census relation.

Historical **25 JIT + 9 extern = 34** memberships in 11 source files. Current **25 JIT + 0 extern**. Commit `4d8ac92ea` retired the DeepEP-like proof targets, including both source files that supplied the nine historical extern memberships. All 25 historical JIT roots remain present. There are 17 distinct JIT callees qualified by file (16 names), and three distinct extern callees. This inventory describes edge-level work; a sequential helper occurring inside a distributed target does not make the rest of that target verified.

## Public caller results

The public JIT contract allows compiled functions to call other JIT functions. The binding uses that contract together with the pinned body of each helper. [Triton v3.5.1 JIT documentation, accessed 2026-11-25](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/v3.5.1/python/triton/runtime/jit.py#L910-L921).

The following tests elaborate pasted call sites and compare complete kernels. The supported names below have ordinary sequential meaning at the pinned sites. Whole distributed kernels depend on the other operations they contain.

| Source helper | Client and verification |
| --- | --- |
| `ceil_div` | `with_local_jit_helpers in with_triton_call` and stored `triton_source_procedure` retain the nested tutorial bounds at 198 and 223. Its expression form admits the two scalar names actually read there. The upstream `jit_functions` entry can use `ceilDiv` in a direct assignment. |
| `swizzle_2d` | The public M-group binding preserves the final short group, caller overlap, lexical branch and both ordered returns. |
| `swizzle_2d_by_group_n` | One checked binding implements the identical bodies in AR and RS. A stored and then instantiated procedure matches all three results and its complete independently spelled caller, including reordered keywords. The two swizzles also have public upstream `StatementJitFunction` bindings. |
| `_is_gpu_master` | The predicate in the source `tl.where` compares the sum of the three program IDs with zero. |
| `copy_continuous_kernel`, `add_continuous_kernel`, `transpose_kernel` | `with_triton_call … dist_procedures in triton` checks the three public procedure bindings at the actual statement position. Source-shaped callers compare the complete loop bodies, masked reads and writes, aliases and both conditional destinations. The int32 transpose cases exercise both dimension orders and the two constexpr keywords. |
| `get_element_at` | Both retained callers use the signed int32 helper through `with_local_jit_helpers`. A whole-kernel equality records the generated prefix scan, reduction and lane selection for one combined test kernel. Executable tests cover both branches in the source callers, negative values, signed overflow and an out-of-range index. [#588](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/588) |
| `_is_cta_master` | Rejected pending [the three-axis SIMT tid binding](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/81). |
| Historical local `sync_warp`, `consume_token`, `unpack_b32_v2` | Tests reject the `sync_warp()` statement, the scalar result of `consume_token` and the tuple result of `unpack_b32_v2`, one pinned call shape per extern. The current imported `dl.consume_token` has a different owner, [#79](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/79). |

The complete lexical, alias and diagnostic regressions are in [SourceHelpers.lean](../../tests/lean/dist/SourceHelpers.lean), [ProcedureHelpers.lean](../../tests/lean/dist/ProcedureHelpers.lean) and [ElementHelper.lean](../../tests/lean/dist/ElementHelper.lean). The mechanical closure reaches both master predicates exclusively below the A9 grid-barrier event. A client testing the CTA predicate on its own must await the three-axis thread binding in #81. The three local `triton_dist.jit` memberships fall outside the JIT/extern count: `all_to_all_v_2d_kernel` reaches distributed prefix-scan code (#81/#82); `barrier_all_intra_node_non_atomic` and `barrier_all_intra_node_non_atomic_block` retain their distributed barrier contracts. The grid barrier is the registered A9 event. Its implementation branches, grid-address wrapper and assembly-backed register access remain below that event. The prefix-scan and ring procedures that call distributed primitives are assigned to [#81](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/81) and [#82](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/82) by the [coordinator's triage](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/451#issuecomment-7066611393).

Triton v3.5.1 keeps int32 as the default accumulator and result of sum and cumulative sum. Both use addition. The fork uses signed lane selection, signed 32-bit wrapping after each addition and a forward inclusive scan on axis 0. [Accumulator and sum](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/v3.5.1/python/triton/language/standard.py#L259-L291) · [Cumulative sum](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/v3.5.1/python/triton/language/standard.py#L329-L341).

The typed frontend accepts the receive copy from the signed split load and prefix through the final two-dimensional masked store. For a positive int32 tile width, Triton computes `(n_row + width - 1) // width` with wrapping int32 addition and signed division toward zero. The fork widens the signed stop calculation for the core loop and binds the source induction variable as int32 on each trip. Within a straight-line body, ordinary assignments and memory operands retain that width through aliases, parentheses, and either operand order of addition, subtraction, multiplication, truncating division and remainder. Each arithmetic result wraps before the next operation. Adding a displacement to a pointer retains the full address. An index-dependent expression with unknown integer promotion or unsupported control flow produces a diagnostic. The client compares the whole tail to explicit casts, reads back the BF16 destination including masked cells, and checks the signed stop independently. The contract assumes valid active addresses and source-valid constexpr dimensions. In particular, a symbolic tile width must satisfy `0 < width < 2^31`, and constexpr operands promoted to int32 must fit that type. [Pinned receive copy](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Triton-distributed/blob/7908e4ea9010bb2238f9f05b28c904fd4b71c60a/python/triton_dist/kernels/nvidia/all_to_all_single_2d.py#L94-L112) · [Triton cdiv](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0add68262ab0a2e33b84524346cb27cbb2787356/python/triton/language/standard.py#L32-L41) · [Range induction type](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0add68262ab0a2e33b84524346cb27cbb2787356/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L1183-L1203) · [Integer scalar promotion](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0add68262ab0a2e33b84524346cb27cbb2787356/python/triton/language/semantic.py#L169-L203) · [Signed division](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0add68262ab0a2e33b84524346cb27cbb2787356/python/triton/language/semantic.py#L311-L322).

Full-root transcription also requires the send root’s `libshmem_device.putmem_nbi_block` at line 67 and the receiving root’s CTA barrier at line 93. [Whole-root tracking](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/181) · [Original diagnostics](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile-2/issues/588#issuecomment-7169427848).
